h1: IT equipment recycling with secure data destruction
lead: When you upgrade your IT, BRS takes care of the old equipment. We recycle hardware responsibly and erase confidential data first.
card_blurb: Responsible recycling of retired IT hardware, with secure data destruction before disposal.
meta_title: IT Equipment Recycling and Data Destruction | BRS
meta_description: BRS recycles retired IT hardware and handles secure data destruction, keeping electronic waste out of landfills when you upgrade your systems.
overview: Most organizations upgrade their IT every few years as systems become obsolete. The old hardware should not simply be thrown away.
BRS handles your retired IT equipment. We recycle it responsibly and make sure confidential data is erased before the hardware leaves your hands.

benefits.title: Less waste in landfills
benefits.text: Recycling keeps electronic waste out of landfills.

benefits.title: Lower pollution risk
benefits.text: Electronics can contain heavy metals such as cadmium, lead and mercury, and should not be dumped.

benefits.title: Data protection
benefits.text: Private emails and confidential files are removed before recycling.

included: Hard drive destruction quotes on request

process.title: Request a quote
process.text: Tell us what equipment you are retiring.

process.title: Destroy data
process.text: Storage devices are wiped or destroyed so information cannot be recovered.

process.title: Recycle or reuse
process.text: Equipment is recycled responsibly, and usable devices can be passed on.

who_for: Offices retiring old servers and computers
Businesses with confidential data on old hardware
Companies that want to keep electronic waste out of landfills

faq.q: Is deleting files enough before recycling a hard drive?
faq.a: No. Deleted data can still be retrieved with recovery tools, so storage devices need to be wiped or destroyed.

faq.q: Why not throw old IT equipment in the trash?
faq.a: It adds to landfill waste, and electronics contain chemicals such as mercury, beryllium and cadmium that can reach water and air.
It can be. Working equipment may go to people who can use it, instead of being discarded.
